desc: Read the input values N, M, S, T and the list of edges to construct the adjacency list for the graph.
Perform a Breadth-First Search (BFS) starting from vertex S to calculate the shortest distance to vertex T.
Check if the distance is 1; if so, print -1 because the pieces block each other on a direct edge.
If the distance is greater than 1, calculate the result as $1 + 2 \times \text{distance}$ and print it.
Ensure the code handles large inputs efficiently within the given constraints ($N, M \le 2 \times 10^5$).

Implement the solution: Read input, build graph, compute degrees, run BFS to find shortest path and nodes on it, apply the logic derived (D=1 case vs D>1 case with degree checks), and print the result.
Refactor the solution to correctly implement the logic derived:
**Case D=1**: If `dist(S, T) == 1`, check if `degree[S] > 1` or `degree[T] > 1`. If true, output `3`. Else, output `-1`.
Check if `degree[S] > 1` or `degree[T] > 1`. If true, output `2 * D`.
If not, check if there exists any node `v` on *any* shortest path from S to T such that `degree[v] > 2`.
To do this efficiently: Run BFS from S to get `dist_S` and from T to get `dist_T`. A node `v` is on a shortest path if `dist_S[v] + dist_T[v] == D`.
